title: Ban on data centers (initiated ordinance)
target_project: Project Milo (near Deer Creek Golf Course)
summary: Citizen-initiated ordinance prohibiting the construction of any data center within city limits, including converting existing buildings. No megawatt threshold: the only outright ban among Ohio's November measures. Council had already adopted a 12-month moratorium.
ballot_text: Shall the ordinance to approve or reject a ban on data centers within the city limits, be passed? (Ohio Secretary of State listing and Trumbull County BOE running list.) The ordinance defines a data center as "any facility that primarily contains electronic equipment used to process, store, and transmit digital information" and also bars converting an existing building into one (fragment per WKBN; full ordinance text not retrieved).
notes: Issue number not yet confirmed; check Trumbull BOE sample ballot. Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file.
results_expected: Usually election night, from the Trumbull County Board of Elections.
plain_summary: Bans building any data center in Hubbard, of any size, including turning an existing building into one.

title: Charter amendment banning data centers (an organization's own facility under 7.5 MW is exempt)
target_project: Thor Equities proposal south of Rittal
proponents: Conserve Ohio / Nicole Nawman petition (400+ signatures)
summary: Adds Section 8.07 to Article VIII of the city charter prohibiting construction of data centers in the city, with an exemption for small privately owned facilities serving a single organization with peak demand under 7.5 MW. Council rescinded its data-center zoning allowance in June and adopted a 12-month moratorium; Thor Equities sued in federal court. A recall of the mayor is on the same ballot.
ballot_text: City of Urbana, Proposed Charter Amendment. A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article VIII of the Charter of the City of Urbana be amended to add Section 8.07, to read as follows? Article VIII, Section 8.07. Prohibition of a Data Center. (A) the construction of a data center is hereby prohibited. (B) as used in this Section, "construction" shall mean the erection of one or more buildings, infrastructure, facilities and related activities, which include preparations and modifications for same, for a common purpose. (C) as used in this Section, "data center" shall mean one or more buildings or physical facilities or infrastructure, located on a single real property parcel or on contiguous, adjacent, or otherwise aggregated real property parcels that are used primarily or exclusively for digital information services such as the management, storage, processing and dissemination of electronic data and information, including but not limited to the implementation of artificial intelligence, through the use of computer systems, servers, networking equipment, and related components, including equipment cooling systems, or virtual currency mining. (D) this Section shall not apply to data centers, as defined in this section, whose sole purpose is to serve as a dedicated facility that supports the computing needs of a single organization or enterprise not otherwise engaged in the business of management, storage, processing, and/or dissemination of electronic data and information and which is wholly owned by that enterprise, and which has an aggregate monthly demand or peak load of less than seven-point-five (7.5) megawatts, however derived from any energy source, or a combination thereof. (E) this Section is self-executing. YES / NO
notes: Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file as Charter Amendment: Article VII, Section 8.07 (the petition's Article VII/VIII inconsistency carries through to the state list). Full text from the Champaign County sample ballot (Urbana 3-A), which prints it without an issue number; the ballot reads Article VIII.
results_expected: Usually election night, from the Champaign County Board of Elections.
plain_summary: Writes a ban on data centers into Urbana's city charter, exempting only small private facilities that serve a single organization and draw under 7.5 MW.

target_project: ~300-acre data center proposal (Beatty/Rensch Rd)
opponents: Grove City Council (unanimously opposed)
summary: Creates a mandatory public referendum for any development of 50 or more acres, more than 20 MW peak demand, or more than 500,000 gallons of water per day, with the developer paying election costs. ballot_text: Community Consent Amendment. Amends the city charter to include a new article, Article XI, to establish a mandatory public referendum process as a condition of approval for any proposed development, qualifiable business expansion, or transfer of property ownership that meets or exceeds one of these following thresholds: occupies 50 or more contiguous acres, draws or is designed to draw more than 20 megawatts of electrical power at peak capacity, or consumes or is projected to consume more than 500,000 gallons of water per day; and establishes enforceable community impact standards for any approved facility. Shall the charter amendment, as proposed by initiative, be adopted?

title: Referendum on Resolution 06-2026 (EdgeConneX development agreement)
target_project: EdgeConneX: two data centers and a gas plant on ~195 acres
opponents: Teays Valley Community Alliance (petition, 669 valid signatures)
summary: Referendum on the council's April resolution approving a development and supply agreement term summary with EdgeConneX. The Ohio Supreme Court ordered the petition certified (State ex rel. McNamara-Smith v. Grube, 2026-Ohio-3035). A YES vote upholds the agreement; a NO vote rejects it (though it does not by itself stop construction). EdgeConneX paid the village $3.5M in October.
ballot_text: Referendum on Resolution (By Petition), Village of Ashville. A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. WHEREAS, EdgeConneX intends to obtain permits through the Village of Ashville to construct and operate two data center buildings with ancillary buildings and infrastructure on certain property within the Village (currently Pickaway County Parcel Number D1300350000100 consisting of approximately 195.368 acres); and WHEREAS, EdgeConneX, through an affiliate, also intends to develop and obtain permits through the Ohio Power Siting Board for authority to construct and operate a natural gas behind-the-meter power generating facility at the property; and WHEREAS, the Village of Ashville and EdgeConneX want to memorialize a framework and timeline, for disclosure of Energy Center parameters, studies, and EdgeConneX's paid support to the Village, the Township, and the School District, through a Term Summary; and WHEREAS, using this Term Summary, the Village of Ashville and EdgeConneX will negotiate and agree to a Development and Supply Agreement that must be approved by Council for the Village of Ashville; and WHEREAS, Council for the Village of Ashville now wants to kick off this project by approving the Term Summary. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the Village of Ashville, County of Pickaway, State of Ohio: Section One. Council for the Village of Ashville hereby approves the Development and Supply Agreement Term Summary attached hereto as Exhibit A. Section Two. It is hereby found and determined that all formal actions of this Council concerning and relating to the passage of this resolution were adopted in an open meeting of Council and all deliberations of Council and any of the decision-making bodies of the Village of Ashville which resulted in such formal actions were taken in meetings open to the public in compliance with all legal requirements of the State of Ohio. Section Three. All prior legislation, or any parts thereof, which is/are inconsistent with this Resolution is/are hereby repealed as to the inconsistent parts thereof. Section Four. Council declares this to be an emergency measure immediately necessary for the preservation of the public peace, health, and safety of this municipality and for the further reason that Council needs to accept these terms as soon as possible so that this project is not unnecessarily delayed. Wherefore, provided this Resolution receives the required affirmative votes of Council, this Resolution shall take effect and be in force immediately upon passage by Council. Shall the resolution enacting approval of a development and supply agreement term summary with EdgeConneX be approved? Yes / No.
notes: A YES vote is the pro-data-center side. Ballot choices are Yes / No (not For / Against), per the Pickaway County ballot proof for precinct 17 Ashville-East (docs/source-docs/pickaway-county-ballot-proof-ashville-east-p2.webp), which prints the full resolution text above the question. Council introduced Resolution 16-2026 in September to repeal the agreement itself, which could have mooted the referendum; on Sept 22 it put off the vote (Citizen Portal meeting summary, https://citizenportal.ai/articles/10163769/Ohio/Pickaway-County/Ashville/Council-delays-vote-on-repeal-tied-to-EdgeConnects-datacenter-agreement). An earlier note here said the repeal failed at its third reading on Oct 5; no source for that was found on Oct 30. Either way the referendum is on the ballot: NBC4 (Oct 26, 2026, https://www.nbc4i.com/news/your-local-election-hq/ashville-residents-to-vote-on-data-center-referendum/) reports the Nov 3 vote, with YES upholding the agreement and NO overturning it, and the Scioto Valley Guardian (Oct 8, https://sciotovalleyguardian.com/2026/10/08/ashville-receives-3-5-million-from-edgeconnex-ahead-of-referendum/) says it is headed to the Nov 3 ballot. The Pickaway County BOE did not return the research assistant's call (Oct 28-30). Village electors only. Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file with the same question wording. No issue number is printed.
results_expected: Usually election night, from the Pickaway County Board of Elections.
plain_summary: A YES vote upholds the council's agreement with EdgeConneX for two data centers and a gas plant on about 195 acres. A NO vote rejects the agreement, though that alone does not stop construction.

title: Charter amendment banning data centers over 25 MW
target_project: Meta's planned campus on about 607 acres at the Piqua I-75 Business and Industrial Park (two buildings, about 700,000 sq ft), approved by the city commission Nov 3, 2025

summary: Adds Section 138, Prohibition of Construction of a Data Center, to the charter's Miscellaneous Provisions: data center construction is prohibited where aggregate monthly demand or peak load exceeds 25 MW from any energy source or combination; self-executing. The same model language as the 25 MW bans in Trenton and Sunbury. Save Piqua filed it Aug 11 with recall petitions against the mayor and two commissioners; the board of elections questioned whether it met the Aug 5 filing deadline, but it appeared on the Nov 3 ballot. Its effect on the Meta project the city had already approved is unclear.
ballot_text: Proposed Charter Amendment, City of Piqua. Be it Resolved by the People of the City of Piqua that the Charter of the City of Piqua is hereby amended to add Section 138 to Miscellaneous Provisions to read as follows: Section 138 Prohibition of Construction of a Data Center (A) The construction of a data center is hereby prohibited. (B) As used in this Section, "construction" shall mean the erection of one or more buildings, infrastructure, facilities, and related activities, which include preparations and modifications for same, for a common purpose. (C) As used in this Section, "data center" shall mean one or more buildings or physical facilities or infrastructure, located on a single real property parcel or on contiguous, adjacent, or otherwise aggregated real property parcels that: (1) Are used primarily or exclusively for digital information services such as the management, storage, processing, and dissemination of electronic data and information through the use of computer systems, servers, networking equipment, and related components, including equipment cooling systems; and (2) Has an aggregate monthly demand or peak load of greater than twenty-five (25) megawatts, however derived from any energy source, or a combination thereof. (D) This Section is self-executing.

A "High Impact Data Center" is defined as a facility whose primary purpose is the housing, operation, and maintenance of computer servers and related infrastructure that requires a peak electrical load exceeding ten (10) megawatts or a daily water draw exceeding one hundred thousand (100,000) gallons. This term includes server farms, colocation facilities, AI training facilities, cryptocurrency mining operations, and similar high-density computing facilities. The prohibition would apply to all zoning districts within the City. Violations would be subject to civil and criminal penalties under the City of Emporia Zoning Regulations. target_project: Proposed ~250,000 sq ft, up-to-50 MW data center
proponents: Monterey Park City Council (Resolution 2026-R6, adopted 5-0 on March 4, 2026)
summary: Amends the General Plan land-use element to prohibit data centers citywide; changeable only by a future public vote. Widely described as the first voter-approved permanent data center ban in the country.
ballot_text: Proposition to Prohibit Data Centers in Monterey Park. Shall the ordinance amending the City of Monterey Park General Plan to prohibit data centers citywide to protect air quality, drinking water resources and public health; prevent impacts to electricity and water rates; with the prohibition of data centers continuing until ended by voters, be adopted? YES / NO.
result_note: Passed 88.3% yes (10,388 to 1,372), final LA County count (results last updated June 26, 2026).
notes: Placed by the City Council under Elections Code section 9222 (Resolution 2026-R6, adopted 5-0 on March 4, 2026; docs/source-docs/monterey-park-2026-R6.pdf), captioned the Community Act Prohibiting Data Centers and consolidated with the June 2 primary. Exhibit A adds a citywide data center prohibition to the Land Use and Urban Design Element adopted by Measure JJ (2020).
plain_summary: Bans data centers citywide through the General Plan, so only a future public vote can lift the ban.

title: Voter approval required for large tax incremental districts
target_project: Vantage Data Centers / OpenAI-Oracle Stargate campus and the $458M TID No. 5
opponents: Metropolitan Milwaukee Association of Commerce and others (suit dismissed Oct 19, 2026)
summary: Bars the city from creating or approving a tax incremental district with a projected base value of $10 million or more, or project costs over $10 million, without voter approval. Prospective only; does not affect the Vantage campus already under construction.
ballot_text: Shall the City of Port Washington adopt the proposed ordinance, which, if adopted, would bar the City from creating or approving a Tax Incremental District that requires a large capital expenditure, or with a base value projected to or exceeding $10,000,000.00, or project costs exceeding $10,000,000.00 [...] (remainder, per coverage: unless approved by city electors at a referendum; verbatim excerpt per WTMJ's voter guide, cut off in the source)
result_note: Passed 66.4% yes (2,710 to 1,371), unofficial Ozaukee County count.
notes: Called the nation's first anti-data-center referendum. An Ozaukee County judge dismissed the business groups' suit against the ordinance on Oct 19, 2026; an appeal is possible.
plain_summary: Requires voter approval before the city creates a tax incremental district with $10 million or more in value or project costs. It applies only to future districts, not the Vantage campus already being built.

title: Advisory: support utility infrastructure for a large data center?
target_project: Cloverleaf Infrastructure land scouting

ballot_text: Advisory question, beginning with Should, asking whether the Village should authorize, support, participate in or facilitate municipal utility infrastructure and related improvements tied to a large-scale data center development within or affecting the Village. plain_summary: Non-binding question on whether the village should build or support utility infrastructure for a large data center.

title: Bond and noise guarantee for hyperscale data centers seeking tax breaks
target_project: Province Group proposal (village declined its abatement/PILOT request in July)
summary: Citizen-initiated ordinance requiring any hyperscale data center developer (over 10,000 sq ft, over 5,000 servers, or over 50 MW) that seeks a tax abatement, PILOT or other special tax designation to first deposit a bond or escrow equal to at least the projected tax revenue over the project's 31-year life plus projected salaries for 200 full-time employees, with annual make-whole payments if projections fall short and assessments for environmental, standard-of-living or property-value effects. Also requires a noise guarantee of 50 dB by day and 45 dB overnight with council-set fines. Conditions the deal rather than banning the building.
ballot_text: 16 Proposed Ordinance (By Petition) Perry Village. A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. The Proposed Ordinance amends Chapter 133.01 “Established; Power and Duties” of the Codified Ordinances of the Village of Perry regarding the duties of the Village Fiscal Officer before signing Village agreements with a hyperscale data center involving tax abatements, PILOT Programs, or any special tax designation. Shall the proposed ordinance amending Chapter 133.01 "Established; Power and Duties" of the Codified Ordinances of the Village of Perry be adopted? Yes / No.
notes: Found Oct 15 as the jurisdiction missing from the earlier list; with Piqua (moved to Feb 2027) it reconciles Ballotpedia's 21 measures / 18 jurisdictions. Confirmed as Issue 16 on the Lake County certified issues list (docs/source-docs/lake-county-issues-11-3-26.pdf); full ordinance text fetched Oct 16 (docs/source-docs/perry-village-ordinance-full-text.pdf, scanned petition, OCR applied). The ordinance defines a hyperscale data center as one exceeding 10,000 sq ft, 5,000 servers or 50 MW; threshold_mw records the MW trigger only.
results_expected: Usually election night, from the Lake County Board of Elections.
plain_summary: Requires any hyperscale data center that seeks a tax break in Perry to first post a bond at least equal to its projected tax revenue plus the pay of 200 full-time workers, and to keep noise under 50 decibels by day and 45 at night. It sets conditions rather than banning data centers.

title: Zoning amendment banning data centers of 25,000 sq ft or more
target_project: Pre-emptive (no project pending)
summary: Permanent zoning amendment that defines a data center as a facility with 25,000 square feet or more of floor area plus associated impervious surfaces, and prohibits it in every zoning district; smaller accessory server rooms are exempt. The Select Board chose a November vote over a moratorium in June and approved the ballot question 3-0 on Aug 18, 2026. A Comprehensive Plan amendment is Question 1 on the same ballot.
ballot_text: Question 2. Shall an Ordinance entitled "Proposed Zoning Ordinance Amendment to Define and Prohibit Data Centers" be enacted?
notes: Polls 8 am to 8 pm at North Berwick Elementary School. Ballot text from the town sample ballot (docs/source-docs/north-berwick-me-sample-ballot-nov-2026.pdf); full amendment text and intent in docs/source-docs/north-berwick-me-referendum-questions-nov-2026.pdf and the town election newsletter (docs/source-docs/north-berwick-me-election-newsletter-nov-2026.pdf). Origin: Select Board minutes of June 2 and Aug 18, 2026 (docs/source-docs/north-berwick-me-select-board-minutes-2026-06-02.pdf, docs/source-docs/north-berwick-me-select-board-minutes-2026-08-18.pdf). The town clerk counts and posts a scanned return, usually the next morning (Nov 2025 and June 2026 precedents); Maine's Secretary of State does not report local questions.
results_expected: The town clerk usually posts the count the morning after the election.
plain_summary: Bans data centers of 25,000 square feet or more from every zoning district in North Berwick; smaller server rooms that support another use are still allowed.

title: 180-day moratorium on data center development and permitting
target_project: Pre-emptive (no project pending)
summary: A 180-day moratorium on accepting, processing or approving building applications, site plans, permits or other approvals for any data center, with no size threshold; routine upgrades to existing telecommunications facilities are exempt. It takes effect on passage. The Selectboard signed the ordinance for the ballot on Sept 14, 2026; no project has been proposed.
ballot_text: Article 2. Shall an ordinance entitled "Town of Peru Temporary Moratorium of the Development and Permitting of Data Centers" be enacted to allow the Selectboard and the Planning Board adequate time to study the impacts of data processing facilities on local water usage, electrical grid capacity, noise levels, and environmental and Government resources. [Wording as published by Ballotpedia; the town warrant and sample ballot were not online as of Oct 31.]

title: Retroactive 180-day moratorium on data centers of 100,000 sq ft or more
target_project: Pre-emptive (no project pending)
proponents: Board of Selectmen (5-0) and Planning Board (7-0)
summary: A moratorium on siting, building or operating data centers of 100,000 square feet or more (floor area plus impervious surfaces), and on accepting or approving applications for them. It is retroactive to June 16, 2026 and runs 180 days from that date, so unless extended it lapses in mid-December, about six weeks after the vote. Residents asked for the pause at a June 16 hearing; both boards recommended it unanimously in September.

notes: Polls 8 am to 8 pm at the Wells Junior High School gym. Ballot text from the official sample ballot (docs/source-docs/wells-me-sample-ballot-nov-2026.pdf); ordinance text in Appendix 1 of the warrant (docs/source-docs/wells-me-warrant-nov-2026.pdf, https://wellstown.org/DocumentCenter/View/8514). Origin: Selectmen minutes of June 16 and Sept 1, 2026 (docs/source-docs/wells-me-selectmen-minutes-2026-06-16.pdf, docs/source-docs/wells-me-selectmen-minutes-2026-09-01.pdf). The mid-December expiry is counted from the warrant's June 16 start; the warrant gives no end date. The town clerk posts a scanned return, usually the next morning.
results_expected: The town clerk usually posts the count the next day.
plain_summary: Pauses data centers of 100,000 square feet or more in Wells for 180 days, backdated to June 16, 2026, so the pause ends in mid-December unless the town extends it.

target_project: Pre-emptive. In 2025 Boundless Power asked about a roughly $5 billion data center on the town-owned Old Ferry Road parcel by the former Maine Yankee plant; the town says no proposal is under consideration.

notes: Polls 8 am to 8 pm at the Wiscasset Community Center. results_expected: The town usually posts unofficial results the morning after the election.
plain_summary: Pauses applications for new or expanded data centers in Wiscasset for six months, starting with applications filed on Nov 3; the Select Board can extend it.

title: Charter amendment requiring independent review before approving large industrial projects
target_project: Applied Digital's Polaris Forge 2 AI campus next to Harwood (about $3 billion, 280 MW, approved Sept 2025). The amendment reaches only approvals not yet final, so in practice it would govern expansions and future projects.
proponents: Voices of Harwood (Mike Swartz and others; 81 petition signatures)
opponents: Mayor Blake Hankey; Applied Digital; Concerned Citizens of Harwood
summary: Initiated amendment adding Article X to the home rule charter: before approving an industrial project over set thresholds (100 MW of peak demand, 100 acres or 50,000 gallons of water a day on their own, or lower combined thresholds), the city must commission independent professional review billable to the applicant, open the records, hold a public hearing and adopt written findings. Data processing facilities are named in the definition. Residents organized after the city approved Applied Digital's campus in 2025 under non-disclosure agreements.
ballot_text: This initiated Home Rule Charter Amendment, published in The Forum on August 25, 2026, would add a new Article X to the Home Rule Charter of the City of Harwood, North Dakota. The initiated amendment would impose additional significant requirements on the City of Harwood for certain development or building projects within the City. These requirements would place new limitations and obligations on how the City evaluates, approves, and administers development or building projects. The full publication in The Forum on August 25, 2026, outlines the specifics of those requirements. The full financial and operational consequences of the initiated amendment cannot presently be determined. The estimated fiscal impact of this measure is unknown. [Wording as published by Ballotpedia; the Cass County sample ballot was not retrieved.]
notes: Polls close 7 pm Central. Full Article X text: docs/source-docs/harwood-nd-charter-amendment-article-x.pdf (city PDF, 16 scanned pages). Council discussion of the petition: docs/source-docs/harwood-nd-council-minutes-2026-06-01.pdf. Ballotpedia says the council placed it; the ballot title calls it initiated and the city minutes and InForum (Sept 8, 2026) describe a citizen petition, so origin is citizen_petition. The ND Secretary of State results feed lists it as contest 1844, "City of Harwood Home Rule Charter Amendment Harwood"; the same ballot has a Harwood sales tax measure (contest 1830). casscountynd.gov blocks scripts (Akamai). North Dakota has no voter registration.
results_expected: Usually election night, from the North Dakota Secretary of State.
plain_summary: Requires Harwood to commission an independent review, paid for by the developer, and to hold a public hearing and adopt written findings before approving large industrial projects such as data centers (100 MW, 100 acres or 50,000 gallons of water a day). It would apply to expansions and future projects, not the Applied Digital campus already approved.

title: Advisory: should the town pursue a data center ban in its Master Plan review?
target_project: Pre-emptive (no project pending)
summary: Non-binding question asking whether an express prohibition of data centers anywhere in the town should be pursued as part of the re-examination of Belvidere's Master Plan; YES means pursue the ban. Per the question's explanation, data centers are not a permitted use in any zone today but are not expressly prohibited, so a developer could seek a variance. The town council discussed the question in June and had the town attorney draft the resolution placing it on the ballot (NJ.com).
ballot_text: TOWN OF BELVIDERE NON-BINDING REFERENDUM QUESTION: YES OR NO Should the prohibition of data centers anywhere within the Town of Belvidere be pursued as part of the re-examination of the Town’s Master Plan? EXPLANATION: The development of a data center within the Town has the potential to generate significant tax revenue. At the same time, concern has been raised with respect to data centers utilizing excessive amounts of water and electricity as well as generating excessive noise from roof-mounted HVAC units. At present, data centers are not a permitted use in any zone within the Town. However, data centers are not an expressly prohibited use, and a data center developer could make application for variance relief. A YES vote would mean that you are in favor of expressly prohibiting data centers as an allowable use within the Town that would completely prohibit the ability of a data center to be built within the Town and eliminate any potential tax revenue from such a development. A NO vote would mean that you are not in favor of expressly prohibiting data centers and are in favor of retaining the ability of the Town’s Planning Board or Board of Adjustment and its professionals to consider a future application for a data center and potentially approve the application, with appropriate conditions.
notes: Added Nov 4, 2026, after Semafor's Nov 4 map showed a non-binding dot on the Delaware River at Belvidere; Ballotpedia's list does not include it. Polls close 8 pm Eastern. Ballot question and explanation verbatim from the Warren County Clerk's Belvidere Municipal Question page (docs/source-docs/warren-county-nj-belvidere-public-question-2026.txt), read in the desktop app's browser because warrencountyvotes.com gives scripts an Akamai Access Denied page; the county's touchscreen sample ballot heads it Municipal Public Question, Town of Belvidere Question. New Jersey governing bodies place non-binding questions themselves (N.J.S.A. 19:37-1); the resolution number was not found. Results: the clerk's unofficial summary report, contest "Town of Belvidere Question" (docs/source-docs/warren-county-nj-2026-general-unofficial-summary-belvidere.txt), entered by hand on the sheet.
results_expected: Election night, from the Warren County Clerk's summary results PDF. Late mail ballots and provisionals are added before the county certifies.
plain_summary: Non-binding question asking whether Belvidere should pursue an outright ban on data centers when it re-examines its Master Plan. Data centers are not allowed in any zone today but could still seek a variance.

title: Zoning ban on data centers in all districts

title: 12-month moratorium on data center permits and approvals
target_project: Tom Moulton's plan to convert a vacant 200,000 sq ft warehouse in the Nottingham Business Park off Route 4 into a data center, withdrawn May 27, 2026

ballot_text: Shall the Town of Nottingham adopt a Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers Ordinance pursuant to RSA 674:23, which would prohibit the acceptance, processing, approval, or issuance of permits or approvals for the establishment, construction, expansion, or operation of data centers within the Town for a period of twelve (12) months, to allow the Town time to study potential impacts and develop appropriate zoning regulations?
